card: Reduces polling sleep intervals in functional test framework sync helpers (sync_blocks and sync_mempools) from 1.0s to 0.05s, and increases RPC readiness polling from 4/s to 20/s. Tests currently waste time sleeping after operations have already finished, slowing down test runs and CI turnaround. The author reports wall-clock reductions of 13% locally and 7% to 15% across various non-CLI CI test jobs. No dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Enforced keyword-only parameters for wait and subsequent arguments in sync_blocks and sync_mempools.
evidence: Author reports local test suite wall-clock time dropped from 110.8s to 96.4s (-13%) and accumulated CPU time dropped from 1715s to 1369s (-20%)

Author's CI job runs showed runtime reductions across platforms: Windows native down 14% (1456s to 1252s), 32-bit ARM down 11% (776s to 690s), macOS down 9% (1287s to 1175s), and previous releases down 15% (930s to 786s)
problem: Functional tests spend idle time waiting for conservative 1-second sleep intervals to elapse even when node state synchronization or RPC readiness completes in milliseconds, unnecessarily prolonging CI and local test execution times.

risk.why: A bug in wait timeouts or excessive polling rate could cause test flakiness or high CPU usage during test suite runs, with no effect on production code.

summary: Increases the polling frequency in the Python functional test framework for node synchronization helpers and the RPC readiness wait loop. In sync_blocks and sync_mempools, the default sleep interval between checks drops from 1 second to 0.05 seconds and subsequent arguments are made keyword-only. In wait_for_rpc_connection, the polling frequency increases from 4 to 20 times per second and replaces iteration count with a monotonic clock timeout check.
